content: Sucralfate is a medication prescribed to treat ulcers. It works by adhering to the damaged ulcer tissue, forming a protective barrier that shields it from stomach acid and digestive enzymes, allowing the ulcer to heal. In some cases, sucralfate may be prescribed for other conditions. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Sucralfate is available in both tablet and liquid forms, and it is taken orally. Typically, it is administered four times a day: one hour before meals and at bedtime. It is important to take sucralfate on an empty stomach, either two hours after eating or one hour before eating. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you need clarification. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. If you are using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before measuring your dose. For the medication to be effective, it must be taken consistently. It may take up to eight weeks for ulcers to fully heal. In addition to treating ulcers, sucralfate is sometimes used to protect the stomach lining in patients taking aspirin or to manage mouth sores caused by cancer chemotherapy. If you are considering sucralfate for these or other conditions, discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. Before starting sucralfate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to sucralfate or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially antacids (e.g., Mylanta, Maalox), anticoagulants like warfarin (Coumadin), antibiotics such as ciprofloxacin (Cipro) or tetracycline (Sumycin), and other drugs like digoxin (Lanoxin), phenytoin (Dilantin), or ketoconazole (Nizoral). If you are taking any of these medications, avoid taking them within two hours of sucralfate. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of heart disease, kidney disease, or diabetes. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, let your doctor know. If you become pregnant while taking sucralfate, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose of sucralfate, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Sucralfate may cause mild side effects, such as constipation, abdominal pain, or gas. To minimize these effects, consume a high-fiber diet that includes fruits, vegetables, salads, and bran, and drink plenty of fluids. However, if you experience severe side effects, such as passing red or black stools or vomiting material that is bright red or resembles coffee grounds, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store sucralfate in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about disposal. It is important to keep all appointments with your doctor and undergo any recommended laboratory tests to monitor your response to sucralfate. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Sucralfate is also marketed under the brand name Carafate®.
